status: DRAFT: freeze by committing this file and recording `git hash-object prereg-friend.json` plus the date in STEER.md BEFORE the first run that counts. Any later edit makes a new version.
scope: Two readers, two networks, one hot key. Can falsify H1 (safety) in the field and establish whether the peer path works across real NATs. Cannot support H2 (efficiency): two readers is far below the simulated audience and the peer-share ceiling with two readers is 50 %.

runs.what: home network to home network, default ICE (STUN only unless TURN is already configured)
friend tethered to a phone hotspot (carrier NAT), default ICE
relay forced on both sides with &relay=1; only if TURN is configured on the deployment

design.repeat: Each required run twice. A hypothesis passes only if both repeats pass.

validity.note: A run that breaks any of these is VOID (repeat it), not a fail. A safety violation found in a void run is still reported.

S1.text: No admitted read is staler than delta + epsilon.
S1.rule: For every 200 read of version v started at publisher time T: T - ack(v_next) <= 6000 + reader clock uncertainty + writer clock uncertainty + guard, where v_next is the lowest acknowledged version above v.

S2.text: No reader observes a version lower than one it already observed.

S3.text: Fail-closed must not mean unusable: failed reads (non-200) stay rare.

F1.text: A DataChannel opens between the two networks.
F1.relayCounts: PASS-RELAY: reported separately because relayed bytes are billed bytes

F2.text: A peer-only read is answered by the peer inside the worker's peer deadline.

F3.text: Organic reads move payload bytes over the peer path.

F4.text: Renewal proofs arrive from the peer, not only from origin.
F4.needs: X-Nodex-Renewal header (preferred) or the Service Worker request log from owner-observe.mjs; otherwise NOT MEASURED

F5.text: Latency stays usable on a real WAN.

predictions.note: Written before any run, so the result can surprise.
predictions.S1_S2: Pass. If S1 fails, suspect the /api/time fallback anchoring before suspecting peers.
predictions.F1: R1 connects as srflx. R2 fails to connect without TURN (carrier NAT is usually symmetric).
predictions.F2: Fails or is marginal on R1 when peer RTT exceeds about 50 ms: a 48 kB payload over a fresh SCTP channel needs several round trips and the complete deadline is 200 ms (OPERATIONS.md:43).
predictions.F3: Below 0.15: both readers notice a new version in the same second and both go to origin.
predictions.F4: Passes if F1 passes: a proof is under 1 kB and one round trip.

decision.S fail: H1 is falsified in the field. Stop all positioning work; fix and re-run.
decision.S pass, F1 fail on R1: The peer transport is not field-viable between ordinary home networks. Ship the guard and the detached proof over the CDN only.
decision.S pass, F1 pass, F2 or F3 fail: Peers connect but do not carry bytes under the current deadline and trigger logic. Keep peers behind a flag; measure the deadline before any byte claim.
decision.all pass: Proceed to the simulator arms in STEER.md section 5, then a 10 to 20 reader run. Two readers still prove nothing about cost.
